messages:
mike: noticing weird churn on gpu-prod this morning — HPA spikes, CA adds nodes, then pods bounce and VPA recommends lower resources. latency SLOs get hit and cost climbs. anyone seen this pattern?

sara: saw something similar in eu-west1 last week. preemptible GPUs in the warm pool caused pod evictions during CA scale-down, tail latency jumped. :frowning: 

nate: can you paste `kubectl get hpa -n inference` and `kubectl describe vpa -n inference`? also autoscaler events/logs would help.

mike: sure — from prod right now:
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME            REFERENCE                    TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
model-scaler    Deployment/model-server     120%/200m  2         20        3
```
and VPA:
```
Name:         model-server-vpa
Mode:         Auto
Recommended:  cpu: 150m  memory: 512Mi
Events:       Update: decreased target for pod model-server-abc -> cpu 200m -> 150m
```

infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale up request for nodepool-gpu-eu-west1 (2 -> 5) triggered at 2024-11-01T12:34:22Z for pods: model-server

anita: this smells like a metrics jitter + control-loop conflict. HPA is driving replicas from QPS spikes (external metric), VPA is simultaneously shrinking requests/limits -> pods become 'underprovisioned' and HPA fires more aggressively.

ops-runner: exact issue: HPA reads external metric 'qps' with 30s scrape window. CA sees sudden pod churn and scales nodepool. CA then later scales down after scale-down-unneeded-time (default 10m) but pods already suffered cache cold starts. plus preemptible GPUs caused evictions.

nate: short-term: set VPA to RecommendationOnly or Off for HPA-managed deployments. long-term: use HPA with stable aggregated metric (e.g., `avg_over_time(qps[2m])`) or add smoothing in metrics adapter.

mike: actionables proposed:
- patch VPA: mode: "Off" for model-server in prod
- change HPA to use behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 for scaleDown and scaleUp policies
- change HPA metric to use averageValue with longer window via adapter
- update CA flags: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` -> maybe bump to 15m to avoid thrash
- create a mixed nodepool: reserved GPUs (non-preemptible) for latency-critical, preemptible pool for batch/burst

sara: for the mixed pool: annotate low-priority pods with `nodeSelector: burst-pool=true` and tolerations for `preemptible=true`. keep inference pods on non-preemptible via nodeAffinity.

nate: testing plan — I'll roll these to staging today. steps:
1) patch VPA yaml -> `mode: Off`
2) patch HPA with
```
behavior:
  scaleDown:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
    policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 20
        periodSeconds: 60
```
3) update metrics adapter to emit `qps_2m_avg` and point HPA to that
4) run load with `wrk -t12 -c400 http://staging-model:8080/predict` for 20m

anita: also add annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"` to model-server pods so CA won't evict them from reserved nodes.

ops-runner: cost note: moving critical pods to reserved GPUs increases base spend ~28% but reduces SLO penalties. we can offset by routing noncritical work to preemptible pool and tighter batching.

mike: thanks. Nate, can you open a short RFC so infra-sre and platform can review the VPA/HPA change? link it here once created.

nate: will do — filing RFC #482: "HPA/VPA control-loop separation + mixed GPU pools". patching staging now, will report back in ~2h. :thumbsup: 

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale up completed for nodepool-gpu-eu-west1 -> nodes added: 3 at 2024-11-01T12:36:05Z

sara: if staging looks good, let's coordinate a midnight deploy for prod to minimize impact.

mike: agreed. let's keep monitoring telemetry for 24h after deploy. add a runbook step to rollback VPA mode if errors > 2% request error rate.

anita: quick note — don't forget to disable VPA recommender side effects (eviction/recommendation autoscale) in cluster role bindings when toggling modes; caught us before.

nate: update: staging load test stable after HPA smoothing and VPA Off. no CA scale-ups during the 20m test and p95 latency stayed within SLO. rolling the change to canary next.

mike: awesome. will post postmortem if prod still sees churn after canary.

ops-runner: adding cost tracking card to the infra board to measure delta after changes.

sara: thanks everyone. closing thread when canary done. :white_check_mark:
